title: Quad Unveils Fiji Port Project and Critical Minerals Pact at New Delhi Meeting
excerpt: Foreign ministers from India, the U.S., Japan, and Australia announced the Quad's first joint infrastructure project and new frameworks for critical minerals, energy security, and maritime surveillance at their May 26 meeting in New Delhi.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Quad's first joint project is a port in Fiji to enhance Pacific infrastructure.
  • A Critical Minerals Framework aims to strengthen supply chains for essential minerals.
  • An Indo-Pacific Energy Security Initiative was launched to stabilize energy markets.
  • Maritime surveillance collaboration will enhance real-time information sharing among Quad nations.
  • A leaders' summit is being planned for 2026 amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.
Fiji Port: A Strategic Move
›First joint infrastructure project by the Quad.
›Located at key Pacific shipping lanes.
›Funded primarily through grants, including a $12 million U.S. grant.
›Aims to counter China's Belt and Road Initiative.
Source: Reuters
  • The Quad announced its first joint infrastructure project — a port in Fiji — to address insufficient capacity in the Pacific Islands and counter China's growing regional influence.
  • A new Quad Critical Minerals Framework will coordinate investment to strengthen mining, processing, and recycling supply chains.
  • The ministers launched an Indo-Pacific Energy Security Initiative and expanded maritime surveillance cooperation.
  • U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said diplomats are working toward a Quad leaders' summit later in 2026.

The foreign ministers of India, the United States, Japan, and Australia met in New Delhi on May 26 for the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting, unveiling the grouping's first joint infrastructure project and signing new agreements on critical minerals and energy security, according to Reuters.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar hosted the meeting alongside U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Japan's Toshimitsu Motegi, and Australia's Penny Wong. The gathering produced four major documents: a joint statement, a fact sheet, a statement on Indo-Pacific Energy Security, and the Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework.

The Fiji Port: A Counter-Bid to Beijing

The headline announcement was a plan to jointly develop port infrastructure in Fiji, marking the Quad's first concrete infrastructure project.

"We are going to be partnering on issues of port infrastructure, in particular in response to insufficient port capacity in the Pacific Islands. We are announcing plans to work with Fiji."

— Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State

The project carries strategic weight. Fiji sits at the crossroads of Pacific shipping lanes, making it a natural logistics hub for trade between Australia, New Zealand, and the wider island chain. Gregory Brown, director of the Alliance Futures Initiative, told Radio Free Asia that the port is a "direct counter-bid" to Beijing's Belt and Road infrastructure investments.

"China lends, the Quad gives," Brown said, noting the project will be funded primarily through grants. "For a country the size of Fiji, that's the entire calculation." The U.S. had already signed a $12 million grant with Fiji through the Millennium Challenge Corporation in March for port feasibility studies. However, Fiji's foreign minister Sakiasi Ditoka told The Hindu that Fiji has yet to formally agree to the project.

Critical Minerals and Energy Security

The ministers launched the Quad Critical Minerals Framework to coordinate investment across mining, processing, and recycling of minerals essential for defense, semiconductors, and aerospace. The initiative is particularly significant for Japan, which has faced Chinese export restrictions on minerals used in these industries.

The joint statement expressed "grave concerns over the use of economic coercion and non-market policies and practices, including arbitrary export restrictions, price manipulation, and disruptions, particularly on critical minerals." The statement did not name China directly but the reference was unmistakable.

The Quad also launched an Indo-Pacific Energy Security Initiative to promote open and stable energy markets, as the U.S.-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions had underscored the region's vulnerability to energy supply shocks.

Maritime Surveillance and Security

The ministers announced the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration (IPMSC) to integrate real-time information sharing across the four nations' maritime systems. India operationalized the Indian Ocean Region programme of the Quad's maritime domain awareness initiative through its Information Fusion Centre in Gurugram.

Strengthening Mineral Supply Chains
›Quad Critical Minerals Framework launched.
›Focus on mining, processing, and recycling.
›Significant for Japan facing Chinese export restrictions.
›Joint statement condemns economic coercion.
Source: Reuters

The joint statement condemned terrorism "in all its forms," referencing the April 2025 Pahalgam attack in India and the December 2025 Bondi Beach attack in Australia. On the South China Sea, the ministers reiterated "strong opposition to any destabilizing or unilateral actions."

Quad Momentum and the Summit Question

The meeting came at a moment of uncertainty. No leaders' summit has been held since September 2024, and tensions between President Trump and Prime Minister Modi over tariffs had strained U.S.-India ties.

"We are beginning to show real achievements and real accomplishments. We are deeply committed to this partnership. It is a linchpin and a cornerstone of our global strategy."

— Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State

Rubio indicated officials would work toward a leaders' summit later in 2026, though no date was confirmed. Premesha Saha of the Asia Society Australia told Reuters: "If the Quad can keep delivering at the ministerial and working levels, it can remain relevant even without regular leaders-level signalling."

Beijing pushed back. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning reiterated that cooperation "should not target a third party" and that China opposes "forming exclusive groupings or engaging in bloc confrontation."

Enhancing Maritime Security
›Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration announced.
›Real-time information sharing among Quad nations.
›Condemnation of terrorism and destabilizing actions.
›Operationalization of maritime domain awareness initiatives.
Source: Reuters

What's Next

The Quad will advance the Fiji port project through feasibility work, implement the critical minerals framework, operationalize the maritime surveillance collaboration, and pursue a leaders' summit. Japan will host a logistics network exercise, and new cooperation on 5G/6G standards, digital identity, and AI governance is planned. The "Pax Silica" initiative — covering critical minerals, semiconductors, and trusted networks — could accelerate investment in India's growing technology manufacturing sector.
